skill.name: shell-scripting
skill.description: Guides users through writing, reviewing, and improving Bash and Zsh scripts with safer patterns and reusable templates.
skill.summary: Create safer Bash and Zsh automation with practical shell scripting guidance.
skill.author: CodingKaiser

security_audit.summary: The static findings are shell syntax examples, reference snippets, and a standard Bash template rather than malicious behavior. No prompt injection, credential theft, hidden persistence, or unauthorized network exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Some examples demonstrate sensitive-looking commands such as reading /etc/passwd or using network tools.
remediation.suggestion: Add short safety notes explaining when these examples are appropriate and warning users not to run commands against sensitive systems without authorization.

remediation.issue: Network examples use curl and wget placeholders that can trigger marketplace scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label all external network examples as placeholders and recommend user confirmation before downloads or POST requests.

content.value_statement: Shell scripts often fail because of quoting, error handling, and portability mistakes. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Bash and Zsh guidance for safer automation.
actual_capabilities: Explains Bash and Zsh script structure, strict mode, traps, and safer word splitting.
Provides patterns for argument parsing, file iteration, input handling, and colored output.
Suggests safer alternatives for common shell mistakes such as parsing ls or leaving variables unquoted.
Includes reference patterns for files, arrays, processes, text processing, dates, network commands, and JSON handling.
Provides a reusable Bash template with options, logging, cleanup, and command dispatch.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete static analyzer for every shell script.
Examples may require adaptation for Linux, macOS, Bash, or Zsh differences.
It cannot guarantee safety for scripts that run commands on production systems.
Network and filesystem examples should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Build reliable automation scripts
use_cases.description: Create Bash scripts with strict mode, argument parsing, cleanup traps, and predictable error behavior.

use_cases.title: Debug fragile shell commands
use_cases.description: Find quoting, globbing, subshell, and pipeline problems in scripts before they affect users.

use_cases.title: Learn safer shell patterns
use_cases.description: Use concise examples to understand file loops, process handling, text tools, and Zsh-specific features.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple Bash script
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a Bash script that takes one directory argument, checks that it exists, and prints each text file safely.

prompt_templates.title: Review a script for common mistakes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this shell script for quoting, error handling, unsafe file loops, and portability issues. Explain each recommended change.

prompt_templates.title: Convert commands into reusable automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these manual terminal commands into a reusable Bash script with help text, dry-run mode, logging, and cleanup traps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production script template
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a robust Bash or Zsh script structure for a deployment workflow, including argument parsing, validation, rollback steps, and safe command execution.

output_examples.input: Review my script that loops over files with for file in $(ls).
output_examples.output: The skill would explain why parsing ls is unsafe, then suggest a glob or find loop that handles spaces and newlines.

output_examples.input: Create a Bash script with verbose mode and cleanup.
output_examples.output: The skill would produce a structured script outline with strict mode, option parsing, logging functions, traps, and a main entry point.

output_examples.input: Make this script work on macOS and Linux.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify commands with different flags, such as stat or date, and suggest portable alternatives or OS-specific branches.

best_practices: Ask the skill to explain why each shell pattern is safe before running it.
Provide the target shell and operating system when requesting scripts.
Review commands that write files, delete files, call networks, or manage processes before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not paste generated scripts into production without reading every command.
Do not use shell snippets with secrets, tokens, or private paths unless you have reviewed redaction and logging behavior.
Do not ask for broad destructive commands when a scoped file or directory operation is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill execute shell commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and templates. Users decide whether to run any command.

faq.question: Can it help with both Bash and Zsh?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Bash best practices and includes Zsh-specific notes for globbing, expansion, and arrays.

faq.question: Is it useful for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common patterns directly and shows safer alternatives for fragile shell code.

faq.question: Can it debug an existing script?
faq.answer: Yes. Paste the script and ask for review of quoting, error handling, portability, and command safety.

faq.question: Does it support production automation?
faq.answer: It can help design production-ready structure, but users must review environment-specific commands and permissions.

faq.question: Why do some examples mention network or system files?
faq.answer: They are reference examples for common shell tools. Review and authorize them before using them on real systems.
